title: Minimum Operations to Make the Array K-Increasing
summary: Given an array arr of n positive integers and a positive integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to make arr K-increasing.
statement: Given an array arr of n positive integers and a positive integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to make arr K-increasing. An array is K-increasing if arr[i-k] <= arr[i] for every index i where k <= i < n. An operation consists of changing any arr[i] to any positive integer. The array is K-increasing if for every i, the value at i is at least as large as the value k positions back.
constraints: arr contains positive integers and k is between one and its length.
After changes, arr[i-k] must be at most arr[i] for every i at least k.
One operation changes one element to any positive value; return the minimum operations.
hints: Indices with the same remainder modulo k form independent sequences that must become nondecreasing.
In each sequence, retain a longest nondecreasing subsequence and change every other value.
Use bisect_right patience tails for each arr[start::k]; add length-len(tails).
Retained values already meet every k-step comparison, and any solution can retain no more than an LNDS in each independent sequence.
editorial: Retained values already meet every k-step comparison, and any solution can retain no more than an LNDS in each independent sequence.

tests.explanation: Only one element can remain in a nondecreasing subsequence, so four changes are needed.
Each residue subsequence is already nondecreasing, requiring zero changes.
